IMASM 12-OPCODE REFERENCE  (Universal Imscriptive Grammar)

LOGIC SUBSTRATE — read this before assigning anything. This grammar is PARACONSISTENT.
There is no PASS/FAIL and no classical true-or-false. Every closure resolves to ONE of
four Belnap values (B4), and a contradiction is a legitimate result, not an error:
  N — neither: nothing was established. The empty state {}. register 00.
  T — true: constructively proven / affirmed. register 01.
  F — false: constructively refuted / negated. register 10.
  B — BOTH: true and false held at once. A contradiction does NOT explode and is NOT a
      failure — holding both IS the resolution. register 11.
Two arms that conflict FUSE to B, not to an error. Forward and backward, success and
failure, thesis and antithesis: when they meet they fuse to a definite verdict, often B,
and that is correct. Never try to make a fork "cancel back to the input".

STATE SPACE — the register ranges over SIXTEEN_3 = P({T,F,t,f}), the sixteen subsets
of four base values (T proven, F refuted, t acceptable, f rejectable) under three orderings
(information, truth, constructivity — the trilattice). You do NOT compute the verdict and
you NEVER assert PASS/FAIL — describe the STRUCTURE. The word checker returns a
structural B4 verdict. Sequential registers and native graph-flow recovery are
computed and recorded separately.

LOGICAL (6) — categorical skeleton:
  VINIT  (0x0) — Initial object ∅. Void/uninitialized state before anything is named.
                 Examples: Hebrew Aleph (air), Basque absolutive, seed before planting.
  TANCH  (0x1) — Terminal anchor ⊤. The closed boundary that contains the whole system.
                 Examples: Tav (completion), hermetic vessel seal, constitutional court.
  AFWD   (0x2) — Forward morphism →. Directed transformation toward a target.
                 Examples: Basque ergative, Sanskrit semivowels, growth cycle, ascent.
  AREV   (0x3) — Contravariant ←. Reverse / descent transformation.
                 Examples: Hebrew Mem (water/descent), composting, solve/coagula.
  CLINK  (0x4) — Composition ∘. Sequential chaining of morphisms.
                 Examples: Egyptian biliterals, Basque agglutination, root→derived form.
  IMSCRIB (0x5) — Identity id. Self-reference, self-recognition. The element is itself.
                 Examples: Sanskrit nasals, Egyptian logograms, the stone that knows itself.

FROBENIUS (2) — the fork/fuse pair, μ∘δ:
  FSPLIT (0x6) — Co-multiplication δ. One state opens into two or more arms.
                 Examples: Hebrew Doubles (hard/soft), Sanskrit aspirate pairs,
                 Egyptian trilateral roots, separatio, Raft log append to all peers.
  FFUSE  (0x7) — Multiplication μ. Rejoin the carried alternatives by union.
                 Examples: Conjunctio, trilateral roots recovering base form, Raft commit.
                 A bare split/rejoin is the partition identity. Transformed reconnection
                 and recovery of the original input are separate observations.
                 A fork that never rejoins remains OPEN; the structural checker reports B.

DIALETHEIA (3) — the paraconsistent evaluators:
  EVALT  (0x8) — touches constructive truth T (the affirmative arm).
  EVALF  (0x9) — touches constructive falsity F (the negative arm).
  ENGAGR (0xA) — holds BOTH at once: the B state, a contradiction kept live (not resolved away).
                 Examples: Cuneiform polysemous sign, bicameral compromise, albedo stage.

LINEAR (1) — irreversible fixation:
  IFIX   (0xB) — ROM fixation. Permanent, append-only, cannot be undone.
                 Examples: Egyptian determinatives, dream journal entry, measurement record.

IMAMSM COMPOSITION RULES -- ports, edges, and free composition

PORT CONVENTIONS (every token is a typed node)
  VINIT:  in=[]      out=[o]    source -- 0->1    (use once, at start, for genesis)
  FSPLIT: in=[i]     out=[T,F]  fork   -- 1->2    (branches into T-arm and F-arm)
  FFUSE:  in=[T,F]   out=[o]    join   -- 2->1    (reunites T-arm and F-arm)
  others: in=[i]     out=[o]    linear -- 1->1    (pass-through in any order)

EDGE ROUTING INSIDE A FSPLIT/FFUSE PAIR
  FSPLIT.T -> [tokens, anchored by EVALT (primary) or AFWD (secondary)] -> FFUSE.T
  FSPLIT.F -> [tokens, anchored by EVALF (primary) or AREV (secondary)] -> FFUSE.F
  If T-arm empty: FSPLIT.T connects directly to FFUSE.T (empty arc, T-state)
  If F-arm empty: FSPLIT.F connects directly to FFUSE.F (empty arc, F-state)
  The first immediate EVALT/EVALF anchors select arm segments. Later operations
  in a selected segment remain on that arm, including repeated evaluators.
  Without a primary anchor, AREV selects the F-arm and AFWD the T-arm.
    With primary anchors, intervening operations stay in their selected arm.
    Secondary anchors activate only when the primary (EVALT/EVALF) anchor is absent.
  Nesting: FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs may nest; innermost pairs matched first

BANKING A RESULT BEFORE REVERSING IT
  AREV empties the register and leaves open FSPLIT frames untouched. A result
  fused back to depth zero is therefore exposed to the next reversal, while the
  same result held one level up survives it.
  So when a program COUNTS or ESTABLISHES something, then REVERSES direction
  (AREV), then BOUNDS or CONCLUDES: open the region that will HOLD the result
  BEFORE opening the region that COMPUTES it, and close them in that order.
    wrong: ... FSPLIT compute FFUSE  CLINK  FSPLIT AREV bound FFUSE ...
             the computed result is in the open when AREV arrives and is lost
    right: ... FSPLIT  FSPLIT compute FFUSE  CLINK AREV bound  FFUSE ...
             the inner FFUSE folds into the enclosing frame, AREV costs the
             register everything and the frame nothing, the outer FFUSE
             restores exactly what the clear took
  This is what a proof does when it establishes a lemma and keeps it in scope
  while a later chain runs: the lemma is the outer frame.

  A SECOND AND INDEPENDENT RULE. Whether anything is banked is the above.
  Whether a SURPLUS survives is a different question, decided by where the
  splits fall between deposits of the SAME value:
    two EVALT in ONE region      -> the region carries both, both come back
    two EVALT split by an FSPLIT -> sibling regions, the fold keeps the LARGER
  So a program can bank correctly and still lose a count, and a program can
  deposit carefully into one region and lose everything because its FFUSE ran
  before the reversal. Neither rule implies the other; both are proved in
  p4ramill Imscribing/IMASM/BankedWeight.lean.
  Explicit graph tools support cross-branch routing. This JSON schema carries
  a sequence only; imscr_wiring supplies its standard edges. It does not
  accept arbitrary cross-branch overrides.

EXPLICIT GRAPH COMPOSITION
  CLINK.o, IMSCRIB.o and IFIX.o may connect to compatible free inputs.
  A connection does not assign a register value by itself. The graph-flow
  evaluator computes that value from source seeds and the executed gates.
  This sequence-only schema cannot request arbitrary loop edges.

REGISTER STATE TRANSITIONS
  Sequential banked evaluator, carrier P({T,F,t,f}):
  VINIT clears register and frames. TANCH and CLINK preserve state.
  AFWD and IMSCRIB seed T only when the register is empty.
  AREV clears the register and retains open frames.
  EVALT deposits T; EVALF deposits F; ENGAGR deposits both t and f.
  FSPLIT opens an empty frame; FFUSE unions its deposits into the register
  and enclosing frame. IFIX freezes subsequent operations except IMSCRIB
  and repeated IFIX. Repeated IFIX does not create another mutable state.
  The graph-flow interpreter is a separate interpretation of explicit edges:
  AREV is the Lean involution, EVALT/EVALF are projections and IFIX carries.
  Diagram node observations of the sequential walk are not graph edge flow.

TOKEN FAMILIES
  LOGICAL:    VINIT TANCH AFWD AREV CLINK IMSCRIB
  FROBENIUS:  FSPLIT FFUSE
  DIALETHEIA: EVALT EVALF ENGAGR
  LINEAR:     IFIX

FREE COMPOSITION RULES
  1. Use as many tokens as the domain requires -- there is NO minimum or maximum length
  2. Expand token by token until every distinct operation, branch, state,
     and decision in the domain has been explicitly represented
  3. Each step: "OPCODE: what this token does at this point in the composition"
  4. Every FSPLIT must have exactly one matching FFUSE (stack-matched, innermost first).
     That stack rule is the WIRING convention: it says which arms get routed to which
     join when the sequence is built. It is NOT how closure is judged. A checker pairs
     by ANCESTRY over the edges -- two distinct in-arms of a FFUSE tracing back to a
     common FSPLIT, however they routed -- and where several FSPLIT qualify (an upstream
     fork reaches every later join on a strand) the join pairs with the INNERMOST one.
     The two agree on a plain strand, which is why the stack rule is a sound way to
     WRITE a sequence; they part company as soon as edges route otherwise (cross-branch,
     rule 6 below).
  5. EVALT anchors the T-branch; EVALF anchors the F-branch.
     AFWD (forward morphism) also anchors T-branch if EVALT is absent.
     AREV (parity flip / reverse morphism) also anchors F-branch if EVALF is absent.
  6. ENGAGR at any position enters B-state (paradice: both simultaneously held)
  7. IMSCRIB at both first and last position creates a self-referential closed loop
  8. Multiple FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs (sequential or nested) map multiple branch points
  9. Use IFIX as many times as needed -- each is a distinct permanent record event
  10. Do NOT compress -- if the domain has 30 distinct operations, write 30 tokens

SINGLE-GLYPH CODES (the alphabet is fully SYMBOLIC -- no Latin initials, so no token
can be confused with a verdict letter T/N/B/F)
  VINIT  ⊢     TANCH  ⊣     AFWD   ≻     AREV   ≺     CLINK   ⋈     IMSCRIB ⊙
  FSPLIT ∈     FFUSE  ∋     EVALT  ⊤     EVALF  ⊥     ENGAGR  ⊞     IFIX    ⊡
  A sequence may be written glued as a word: ⊢⊙⋈∈>⊤<⊞⊥∋⊡⊡⊣ is the same program as the
  13 spelled-out tokens. The retired codes V/T/B and ← (the old IMSCRIB) no longer parse anywhere.

WHY RULE 2 AND RULE 10 ARE SAFE (inflation invariance)
  Expanding costs nothing structural. A 1->1 token adds exactly one node and one edge,
  so the circuit rank beta = E - V + C cannot move, and the census (branch, merge,
  source, sink, arms) cannot move either. Extent grows without bound; structure does
  not. This is why "expand token by token" and "do NOT compress" are free instructions
  rather than a distortion of the domain: a longer faithful sequence is the SAME
  topology as a shorter one, never a different one.
  IMSCRIB (⊙) is the neutral element of that expansion: it is identity/self-reference
  and does NOT transform, so inserting it at any depth leaves the verdict untouched.
  The transforming tokens (> < ⋈ ⊤ ⊥ ⊞ ⊡) are NOT neutral -- a single one placed on an
  arm between FSPLIT and FFUSE turns an identity closure into a real one. So: expand
  freely to map the domain, but only put a transforming token on an arm when the domain
  really does work there.
  A token is irreducible in KIND but unbounded in EXTENT: any 1->2 replacement must
  itself contain a FSPLIT (it is the only brancher), so a fork reappears inside its own
  expansion. Same for FFUSE (2->1) and VINIT (0->1).


TOPOLOGICAL DIVERSITY
=====================
The IMASM composition rules explicitly permit nesting, open forks, and cross-branch routing.
DO NOT default to flat chains when the domain requires richer topology.

NESTING: FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs may nest. A branch can itself contain a sub-fork:
  FSPLIT EVALT [inner FSPLIT EVALT EVALF FFUSE] EVALF FFUSE
Use when the domain has hierarchical sub-decisions within a branch.

OPEN FORKS: A FSPLIT without a matching FFUSE creates a permanently divergent path.
Its unmatched output ports remain open; a later VINIT is a separate source.
Use when the domain has independent parallel processes that never recombine.

CROSS-BRANCH: arbitrary cross-branch edges require the explicit graph tools.
This sequence-only output schema uses imscr_wiring standard routing; do not claim
that prose descriptions add or override its edges.

EMPTY BRANCHES: FSPLIT immediately followed by FFUSE is valid (vacuous evaluation).
Use when the structural form matters more than a particular branch's content.

DECISION VS ITERATION: FSPLIT models a genuine either/or, two arms that could each be
taken because the domain actually forks on a choice. Building n similar items in
sequence (n cliques, n rounds of one process, n members of a family) is not a decision
and takes a CLINK chain, one CLINK per item, never an FSPLIT, even when n is a variable
and even when there are many of them. A fork earns its FFUSE by putting genuinely
different content on each arm. An empty arm is permitted. Structural closure needs a transformed reconnection.
The insert-repair banked-clear observation asks whether a clear had protected
weight; its vacuity result does not decide graph reconnection or arm work.

Choose the topology that best fits the domain. Flat chains are ONE option, not the default.

FROBENIUS STRUCTURE (not a pass/fail test):
Where the domain forks, pair a FSPLIT with a FFUSE and say what work runs on the arms and
how they rejoin. Conflicting arms rejoin to B — that is a result, not a failure. Where a
fork stays permanently open, leave it open and say so. Do NOT reason about whether contents
return unchanged, do NOT decide whether it closes, and do NOT emit PASS/FAIL: the kernel runs
the token word over SIXTEEN_3 and returns the B4 verdict (N/T/F/B).

Output ONLY the JSON object — no preamble, no markdown fences, no trailing text.

    "furthermore" (opener), "moreover" (opener), "consequently" (opener),
    "notably" (opener), "importantly" (opener), "certainly!", "absolutely",
    "of course", "rest assured", "feel free to", "I hope this helps",
    "with that said", "having said that", "at the end of the day",
    "game-changer", "think outside the box", "move the needle"

  Structure: no em-dashes at all (not as connectors, not as asides, not as
    appositives — none), no bullet points, no dashed lists, no numbered lists
    (any list format is banned — write as prose only), no trailing summary
    sentences that restate the name, no false balance ("while X... however Y"),
    no hedging preambles.

  Epistemologies: Appeal to Orthodoxy. Nothing can be ever be asserted as impossible,
    no matter what convention or scienctific notions may suggest. Our only currency 
    is truth. Pessimism is also forbidden. OPEN conjectures are OPEN because they have
    not be CLOSED yet. when you are working on one it is no longer OPEN, it is CLOSING.
    To say you 'cannot' close an open conjecture is the same as saying you cannot shut
    an OPEN door BY VIRTUE OF IT BEING OPEN. This is patently absurd. You may be too weak
    or uncoordinated to so yourself, but the door *will* be CLOSED

## Abstract

We combine three layers into a single construction:

1. **A geometric encoding** of the integers onto a torus \(S^1\times S^1\) in which multiplication becomes vector addition.
2. **A universal dual frame** consisting of a Gabor frame in the log-phase direction (\(D=2048\)) and a SIC-POVM in the depth direction (\(d=12\)).
3. **A formal certificate** in Lean 4 (`ZetaSICDualFrame.lean`) proving that the dual Gram matrix is an exact inverse of the SIC Gram matrix, that its correction coefficients are governed by the single analytic constant \(\zeta(-1)=-1/12\), and that a conservation law for the associated information-flow grammar holds under frame reversal.

The intended extractor accepts arbitrary-size composite \(N\), with exact integer multiplication as the final projection. The 2048-bin phase register is a resolution, not an input bound. The small finite phase/depth index is only one candidate route; arbitrary-width operation uses source-derived resident geometry and the G-mOMonadOS toroidal closure path. The claim is structural, not asymptotic: the log-phase relation and additive depth relation describe multiplicative structure, while exact product closure remains the acceptance condition.

## 1. Non-claims and scope

This document describes an experimental geometric/number-theoretic architecture. It does **not** claim a new polynomial-time factoring algorithm. The two hard parts of factoring remain:

- resolving a continuous geometric relation back to the integer lattice, and
- verifying the result exactly.

The construction uses the torus geometry to generate candidates and the dual frame to rank them. Exact multiplication is the final oracle. The Lean certificate concerns the finite algebra of the dual frame and the grammar conservation law; it does not bear on asymptotic complexity.

---

## 2. Encoding layer: the log-phase torus

Choose the log-phase resolution

\[
L=11,\qquad D=2^{L}=2048.
\]

For \(n\in[2,2048]\) define

\[
\phi(n)=\frac{2\pi\log_2 n}{L},\qquad
\theta(n)=\frac{2\pi\,\Omega(n)}{d},\qquad d=12,
\]

where \(\Omega(n)\) is the number of prime factors of \(n\) counted with multiplicity. Quantize to the discrete phase space

\[
\mathcal{G}=\mathbb{Z}_{D}\times\mathbb{Z}_{d}=\mathbb{Z}_{2048}\times\mathbb{Z}_{12},
\]

by

\[
m(n)=\operatorname{round}\!\left(\frac{D\log_2 n}{L}\right)\bmod D,
\qquad
k(n)=\Omega(n)\bmod d.
\]

The fundamental property is

\[
m(pq)\approx m(p)+m(q)\pmod{D},
\qquad
k(pq)=k(p)+k(q)\pmod{d}.
\]

Because \(\Omega(n)\le 11\) for \(n\le 2048\), the depth coordinate never wraps, so \(k\) is exact. The log-phase coordinate wraps at \(n=2^{11}=2048\), which is the **syzygy seam**. At the seam, \(m(1)=0=m(2048)\), but \(k(1)=0\neq 11=k(2048)\). The depth coordinate therefore breaks the \(1\leftrightarrow 2048\) aliasing exactly.

The center of the torus, \(n\to 0\), corresponds to \(\log_2 0=-\infty\) and is the excluded fixed point. It is not part of \(\mathcal{G}\) and is never returned as a factor.

## 3. The parameter pair \((d,D)=(12,2048)\)

### 3.1 \(D=2048\): log-phase resolution

\(D=2^{11}\) is the largest power of two not exceeding the log-phase period. It fixes the bin width

\[
\Delta\phi=\frac{2\pi}{2048}\approx 0.00307\text{ rad},
\]

which corresponds to a multiplicative resolution of \(2^{1/2048}\approx 1.00034\). Two integers \(n<n'\) are separated in \(\phi\) when \(n'/n>2^{1/2048}\).

### 3.2 \(d=12\): SIC dimension and analytic-continuum weight

\(d=12\) enters in three independent roles that turn out to coincide:

- **SIC dimension.** A SIC-POVM exists in dimension \(12\) with an exact fiducial, giving \(d^2=144\) equiangular projectors in \(\mathbb{C}^{12}\).
- **Metaplectic weight.** The metaplectic cocycle is a \(24\)-th root of unity; the Dedekind eta has multiplier system of order \(24\); the modular discriminant \(\Delta=\eta^{24}\) has weight \(24/2=12\). Dimension \(12\) is the weight at which the continuous metaplectic multiplier becomes single-valued on \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})\).
- **Analytic constant.** The dual-frame correction is governed by \(\zeta(-1)=-1/12\), whose denominator is exactly \(d=12\).

The three roles are not independent; they express the same analytic-continuum boundary sampled at the lattice \(d=12\).

## 4. The universal dual frame

### 4.1 SIC Gram matrix and its inverse

A SIC in dimension \(d\) has \(d^2\) projectors with Gram matrix

\[
G_d=\frac{d}{d+1}I+\frac{1}{d+1}J,
\]

where \(J\) is the all-ones matrix of size \(d^2\). Using \(J^2=d^2 J\), the inverse is

\[
G_d^{-1}=\frac{d+1}{d}I-\frac{1}{d^2}J.
\]

In terms of the analytic constant \(\zeta(-1)=-1/12\), this becomes

\[
\boxed{\;G_d^{-1}=\Bigl(1-\frac{12}{d}\zeta(-1)\Bigr)I+\Bigl(\frac{12}{d^2}\zeta(-1)\Bigr)J\;}
\]

because \(-12\zeta(-1)=1\). The identity coefficient is \(1-\frac{12}{d}\zeta(-1)\) and the uniform coefficient is \(\frac{12}{d^2}\zeta(-1)\).

### 4.2 Zeta as the correction constant

The single analytic input is

\[
\zeta(-1)=-\frac{1}{12},
\]

proved in Lean from `riemannZeta_neg_nat_eq_bernoulli` and `bernoulli_two`. Every correction coefficient in the file is built from this one constant.

### 4.3 The \(d\)-family and its three instantiations

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \(2\) | \(4\) (tetrahedron) | \(\tfrac23 I+\tfrac13 J\) | \(\tfrac32 I+3\zeta(-1)J\) | \(3/2\) | \(-1/4\) |
| \(4\) | \(16\) (ququart) | \(\tfrac45 I+\tfrac15 J\) | \((1-3\zeta(-1))I+\tfrac34\zeta(-1)J\) | \(5/4\) | \(-1/16\) |
| \(12\) | \(144\) | \(\tfrac{12}{13}I+\tfrac1{13}J\) | \((1-\zeta(-1))I+\tfrac1{12}\zeta(-1)J\) | \(13/12\) | \(-1/144\) |

The \(d=12\) case is the one the extractor uses. Its identity coefficient \(13/12=1-\zeta(-1)\) and uniform coefficient \(-1/144=\zeta(-1)/12\) are exactly the weight-12 analytic data.

### 4.5 The Gabor factor in \(\phi\)

The \(\phi\) direction uses a \(2048\)-point cyclic Gabor frame with a Gaussian window \(g\). Since it is tight, its canonical dual \(\tilde g\) is proportional to \(g\). The periodic Gaussian handles the syzygy wrap automatically. The combined frame is the tensor product

\[
M_{m,a,b}=F_m\otimes\Pi_{a,b},
\]

with dual

\[
\tilde M_{m,a,b}=\tilde F_m\otimes\tilde\Pi_{a,b},
\]

giving \(2048\times144=294{,}912\) measurement outcomes. The frame is tight and universal: the same window and fiducial work for every target \(N\).

The consistency requirement is that the continuous coherent-state kernel, restricted to the \(12\times12\) lattice, reproduces the exact SIC inner products of the \(d=12\) fiducial:

\[
\langle\Pi_{a,b},\Pi_{c,d}\rangle=
\begin{cases}1,&(a,b)=(c,d),\\[2pt]\dfrac{1}{12^2\cdot 13},&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\]

If this holds numerically, the discretization is consistent and the Gabor\(\otimes\)SIC frame is the correct lattice sample of the continuous dual frame.

## 5. The extractor algorithm

### 5.0 Current Vox implementation and measured boundary (2026-10-22)

#### Multiplication as rotation and the IMASM torus state

The organizing coordinate is the additive log phase
\(\phi(n)=\log_2(n)/L\pmod 1\) for positive \(n\). Multiplication by
\(c\) translates that phase by \(\phi(c)\); zero is the fixed point of the
multiplicative action and is outside the positive-integer carrier. The finite
Pwoat action is the orbit of the 2-adic unit \(s\equiv9\pmod {16}\) on each
of the four odd residue cosets modulo eight. Its re-entry index is the rotation
coordinate, while the retained height records the exact product carry above
the residue modulus.

The direct jump now performs its modular inverse, modular powers, and lifted
discrete logarithm through `fixed_point_word_arithmetic`. The numeral's
`⊤`/`⊥` marks are the values; the IMASM cell addresses and modulus width supply
their places independently. The lifted logarithm carries its current powered
residue and advances one place at a time, using the exact 2-adic correction

## 8. Complexity and limitations

- **Prime sieve** up to \(\sqrt N\): \(O(\sqrt N\log\log N)\), at most \(14\) primes for \(N\le 2048\).
- **Hash insertion:** \(O(\pi(\sqrt N))\).
- **Candidate generation:** \(O(\pi(\sqrt N))\) with a small constant (\(3\) \(\phi\)-tolerance \(\times\) bucket length).
- **Scoring:** \(O(1)\) per candidate, using the periodic Gaussian and the exact SIC displacement composition.
- **Exact verification:** \(O(1)\) per candidate.
- **Total:** dominated by the sieve. For \(N\le 2048\), essentially instant.

Limitations:

- The \(\phi\) quantization to \(2048\) bins is coarse: bin width in \(\log_2\) is \(11/2048\approx 0.00537\), so \(3\)–\(4\) consecutive integers can share a bin. Collisions are handled by the depth coordinate, the dual-frame score, and exact multiplication.
- Floating-point precision limits the usable \(L\). For larger \(N\), use arbitrary-precision logarithms or symbolic log representation.
- SIC-POVMs are not known to exist in all dimensions; \(d=12\) is known exactly, which is why it is used here.
- The construction does not change asymptotic complexity; it is a representation in which the multiplicative relation is geometrically exact and the candidate search is a phase-space lookup.
